4226c0cb6fe2d113f3efdd190a1877a55bda8c78: Haus im Ennstal offers 123 km of well-marked pistes, a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 47 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Haus im Ennstal's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The altitude of Haus im Ennstal (750 m at the base, 2015 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Haus im Ennstal is clearly on the expensive side: €79 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Haus im Ennstal lives up to its promises. A Northern Alps resort that will suit most skiers without disappointing.

42ff5484e7038002004cad286fc4219eaf7b9839: La Tania is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 25 km of pistes for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. La Tania's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2732 m and a village at 1350 m, snow reliability at La Tania is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strains early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once serious snowfall arrives. A stay at La Tania is clearly expensive: €77 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: La Tania is one of those rare resorts that combines a genuine village, a sincere family atmosphere and runs suited to everyone. It is hard to go wrong with a stay here.
